codeReview.summary: The implementation fully satisfies all feature requirements. The typed entities package is created at the correct path (internal/interfaces/tui/entities/), all 5 entity structs (Agent, AgentNode, Room, RoomMessage, EventRow) are declared with appropriate fields, the EntryKind enum covers all 18 specified kinds with a sentinel EntryKindUnknown, and the ParseEntryKind legacy-string mapper works correctly with case-insensitive lookup. Tests are comprehensive (11 cases) covering constant existence, distinctness, String() output, full legacy-string mapping, case-insensitivity, unknown handling, round-trip consistency, and struct field access. The code is clean, well-documented, and follows project conventions.

issues.description: The existing codebase also uses Kind="plan" (shell_state.go:46) and Kind="seed" (used extensively in tests as a test-only initial kind). These are NOT part of the 18 kinds specified in the feature description, so their absence is correct per the spec. However, the architecture.md's typed-enum design will eventually need to account for them when the legacy ShellState is bridged to the new CockpitState — ParseEntryKind will return EntryKindUnknown for "plan" and "seed" strings. This is acceptable for now since the feature explicitly scoped to '18 current kinds' and the entities package is for the new cockpit (not replacing the legacy ShellState yet).

summary: PASS. The typed entities package is well-implemented and fully satisfies the feature spec. All 18 EntryKind constants are declared as a typed int enum with an Unknown sentinel, all 5 entity structs are present at the correct path, the ParseEntryKind mapper handles all current string values with case-insensitive lookup, and 11 unit tests provide thorough coverage. The code follows project conventions (no IO in the package, pure types/functions, deterministic output). One non-blocking note: the existing legacy codebase also uses "plan" and "seed" kinds which will need attention when bridging the old ShellState to the new CockpitState, but this is correctly out of scope for this feature.
